IF YOU WANT TO BECOME A TOP 1% BACKEND ENGINEER, STOP ADDING MICROSERVICES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES:

Start with a monolith until it hurts.

One deploy, one database, one log stream. Split only when a team or scale boundary forces you.

Every network call is a failure waiting.

Timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers. Assume every dependency will die at 3am.

Make slow things async.

Emails, webhooks, reports. If the user doesn't need it now, queue it and return fast.

IF YOU WANT APIS THAT DON'T BREAK CLIENTS, STOP GUESSING STATUS CODES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES:

200 means done, 201 means created.

Return the resource location with 201. Clients should never guess where their object went.

400 is their fault, 500 is yours.

Validation errors get 400 with field-level messages. Never leak a stack trace with a 500.

Version in the URL, paginate every list.

/v1 today saves you tomorrow. Limit plus cursor beats offset for anything that grows.

IF YOU WANT SYSTEMS THAT SURVIVE TRAFFIC SPIKES, STOP HOPING.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 DEFENSES:

Cache the hot path first.

Profile before optimizing. One cached query at the top endpoint beats ten micro-tweaks elsewhere.

Rate limit everything public.

Per key, per IP, per user. The cheapest outage to prevent is the one an abuser causes.

Load test before launch, not after.

2x expected traffic in staging. Finding the bottleneck at midnight is a choice.
